chosen_rationale: Ground truth verified on disk: public/assets/animation/UAL1_Standard.glb is a real Khronos glTF export with exactly 65 skin joints (names verbatim: root, pelvis, spine_01/02/03, neck_01, Head, clavicle/upperarm/lowerarm/hand_[lr] + full 5-finger chains incl. *_04_leaf, thigh/calf/foot/ball/ball_leaf_[lr]) and exactly 43 clips (incl. the stress set Fixing_Kneeling, PickUp_Table, Push_Loop, Driving_Loop, Sitting_Enter/Idle/Exit/Talking, Crouch_Fwd/Idle_Loop, Jog_Fwd_Loop, Interact, Idle_Talking_Loop, plus A_TPose as the rest reference). The current crew (src/components/Workers.tsx) is literally this raw ~7.6MB mannequin GLB, SkeletonUtils-cloned and per-instance color-tinted — the exact tint-only stopgap all three concepts target. A DECISIVE FACT drove the hybrid: I parsed the bind pose and the bones carry large baked LOCAL rotations (upperarm_l 93.7deg, clavicle_l 102.8deg, thigh_l 165.9deg, pelvis 104.5deg quaternion angles). Rest is NOT a clean T-pose and bone ROLL — not just joint position — governs how mesh must be oriented at each bone. This means the ONLY safe build path is to append the armature unchanged and generate geometry from each bone's EVALUATED world matrix in the bind pose, never from a hand-authored joint-position list. Judging the three concepts against (1) buildability, (2) animation-safety across all 43 clips, (3) house-style fit, (4) role readability: Concept B (5-head, 6.5k tris) risks the childish/cartoon read against the mid-century premium tone (its own risk #3) and is 3x the tri budget the labs proved unnecessary — fidelity is technique, not geometry. Concept C is the safest to bind but its rigid faceted 'wooden artist mannequin' read fights the warm believable studio look and interpenetrates at deep flexion (Sitting_*, Crouch_*, Fixing_Kneeling, Driving_Loop). Concept A has the correct identity (grounded ~7-head, ~2k tris, warm palette, silhouette-first role encoding, painted-ovoid face) but a fully continuous single-skin body is exactly where low-poly skins candy-wrapper and tear at extreme flexion — the non-negotiable risk. The lock is therefore Concept A's IDENTITY (proportions, palette, costume-and-silhouette role read, painted face, ~2k budget) wearing Concept C's DEFORMATION ARCHITECTURE (one mesh island per major bone joined into a single skin, with narrow 1.5-2cm overlapping capsule blend-bands at each joint and fused-paddle hands weighted to hand_[lr] only). That combination delivers the grounded believable crew the milestone wants at the affordable budget, while making first-pass clean binding across all 43 clips near-certain by construction rather than by hope. The architecture kit (13 modules, 3,830 tris unique) and props spec (12 entries, 5,170 tris) are accepted as-authored with minor refinements folded in below; both are already correctly anchored to the real src/lab/materials.ts PALETTE/M and src/lab/heroMaterials.ts HERO/HM/heightToNormal/markTexture/hazardTexture/practical pipeline verified in-repo.
character_bible:
LOCKED CHARACTER: "Grounded Studio Crew v1" — grounded-stylized ~7-head adult film-crew figures, procedurally built in bpy as segment-island shells fitted to the appended 65-bone UAL1 Mannequin in its evaluated bind pose, joined into ONE skinned mesh, role authored into silhouette + costume + prop (tint is the WEAKEST signal), rendered under the existing warm/ACES/RoomEnvironment rig with the function-coded procedural-PBR family. Target ~2.0-2.2k tris LOD0. This REPLACES the raw-mannequin+tint crew in Workers.tsx.

=== NON-NEGOTIABLE RIG PROTOCOL (build order) ===
1. APPEND the armature from UAL1_Standard.glb UNCHANGED. Do NOT add, rename, reparent, re-roll, re-pose, or re-scale any of the 65 bones. Verify on export: skin reports exactly 65 joints, identical names, identical hierarchy. This is the byte-shared guarantee that all 43 clips retarget 1:1.
2. Read every joint's world transform from the EVALUATED bind pose (bpy: armature.pose bind / bone.matrix_world), NEVER from a hand-authored coordinate table. Bones carry baked local rotations (measured: upperarm_l 93.7deg, clavicle_l 102.8deg, thigh_l 165.9deg, pelvis 104.5deg) — mesh orientation must follow the actual bone roll, so all geometry is generated in bone-local space and transformed by the bone's world matrix.
3. Model IN the rest/bind pose (the A-pose implied by those rotations — arms angled down, wrists twisted). Never model in a T-pose then hope it binds.

=== PROPORTIONS (anchored to the measured rig) ===
- Overall height 1.80 m standing; 1 Blender unit = 1 m; +Y up on glTF export. Head unit ~0.255 m => ~7.05 heads (grounded, adult, NOT caricature).
- Anchor heights (world, foot sole = 0.0): pelvis/crotch ~0.92 m, sternum/spine_03 ~1.32 m, clavicle line ~1.40 m, neck base ~1.46 m, chin ~1.55 m, crown ~1.80 m.
- Widths: shoulder ~0.44 m (clavicle x-offset doubled + deltoid flesh), hip ~0.34 m, chest depth ~1.25x hip depth (subtle adult wedge, NOT heroic exaggeration).
- Limb diameters, tapered (NOT sticks): upperarm 0.10 -> wrist 0.055; thigh 0.17 -> ankle 0.075; forearm 0.08; calf 0.12; neck ~0.11.
- Two body sizes ONLY, both from root-scale + a girth multiplier on segment RADII — bone LOCAL translations stay frozen so retarget is 1:1: "standard" 1.80 m girth 1.00; "heavy/older" 1.74 m (root scale 0.967) girth 1.12 on torso/upperarm/thigh radii. No new bones, no moved joints, ever.

=== DEFORMATION ARCHITECTURE (the hybrid safety layer — from Concept C) ===
- Body = ONE mesh island per MAJOR deforming bone, generated at that bone's bind-pose world matrix, then Joined into a single object. Islands (16 major, fingers NOT individually meshed):
  pelvis (hex/box hips spanning pelvis->spine_01), spine as 3 barrel ring-segments split at spine_01/02/03 so bend distributes, neck_01 (short cylinder), Head (ovoid), clavicle_[lr] (short shoulder wedge/deltoid cap), upperarm/lowerarm/hand_[lr] (tapered capsules; hand = one rounded mitten paddle + separate thumb nub), thigh/calf/foot+ball_[lr] (tapered capsules + wedge shoe with a toe break at the ball joint).
- Adjacent islands OVERLAP by ~1.5-2.0 cm at every joint. The overlap is the deformation strategy: a joint rotation rotates a near-rigid chunk about a joint its geometry already surrounds, so no gap can open and no candy-wrapper pinch forms.
- Weights are near-binary: each island ~100% its own bone, with only a 1.5-2 cm blend band across each joint carrying a smooth 2-bone gradient. Max 4 influences, normalized (glTF/Unreal limit). No orphan verts.
- FINGERS: the 20 finger bones REMAIN in the skeleton (bone count stays 65, clips stay valid) but drive a single fused paddle; the mitten + thumb nub are weighted to hand_[lr] and the first knuckle ONLY (index_01/middle_01) — NEVER the leaf bones — so PickUp_Table / Interact / Push_Loop don't splay the mitt.
- NO shape keys, NO correctives, NO cloth sim. Rigid-chunk read at extreme flexion is the accepted stylized signature (management-orbit distance, not close-up).

=== FACE METHOD (Concept A, buildable) ===
- Head = a smooth low-poly ovoid (icosphere-derived, flattened back and a slightly flattened front facet for clean projection), ~4-5 rings, weighted 100% to Head (one rigid island — can never deform-crack).
- Features = ONE procedurally-drawn 512x512 face texture, planar-projected onto the front facet, authored with the EXACT repo pipeline (canvas 2D raster -> albedo, optional heightToNormal for the faintest brow/nose relief; NO Math.random, seeded mulberry32 from src/lab/heroMaterials.ts). Draw: warm skin base, soft brow shadow, eye almonds with a highlight dot (painted, NO eyeball geometry, NO lids), nose shadow + a tiny optional geo nose wedge, mouth line, hairline block, optional painted mustache/stubble (period cue).
- 5-8 seeded texture variants (brow/eye/skin/hair combos) give crowd variety at ZERO extra geometry. Per-instance skin/hair tone via vertex color, deterministic (seeded).
- Additive geo tabs only for silhouette items that must catch light: hair-shell cap, optional glasses ring — 1-3 tiny tabs max. Facial hair is painted, not modeled.
- Realism deliberately capped at "stylized believable" per the house line; cameras stay at crew distance.

=== COSTUME (additive, weighted to EXISTING bones only) ===
Costume is additive geometry snapped to the same joints — NO new bones. Coat/jacket shell = offset torso + upperarm loft weighted to spine + upperarm (same bones as the limb it overlays). Trouser cuffs = offset lower-leg ring. Shoe/boot wedges over foot+ball. Belt ring at pelvis. Tool-belt / holster / apron block weighted to pelvis (apron blends pelvis+spine_01). Rolled-sleeve rings at lowerarm. Headwear parented to Head. Shoulder cable coil weighted to clavicle_l + spine_03. Keep shells SNUG and weighted to the SAME bones as the underlying limb so they never float and clip minimally. Everything low-poly cylinders/boxes/lofts, triangulated on export, no booleans that leave n-gons.

=== VERIFICATION GATE (must pass before sign-off) ===
Headless playback (reuse the lab's capture-*.mjs + window.__lab pattern) of the full 43-clip set, with a mandatory STRESS subset captured per role: Idle_Loop, Walk_Loop, Jog_Fwd_Loop, Fixing_Kneeling, PickUp_Table, Push_Loop, Sitting_Enter, Sitting_Idle_Loop, Sitting_Exit, Crouch_Idle_Loop, Driving_Loop, Idle_Talking_Loop, Interact. Assert: (a) no vertex separates / no NaN, (b) no gap or candy-wrapper pinch at shoulder/elbow/hip/knee/spine, (c) no hat/prop/cable float, (d) acceptable (not gross) self-intersection at deep sit/kneel/crouch, (e) exported glTF still reports exactly 65 bones, unchanged names/hierarchy. Capture proof PNGs per role per stress clip.

=== ISOLATION ===
Visual assets + rig only. No game mechanics, chemistry, aging, career, schedules, economy, LLM. R&D proof, not merge. All deterministic (seeded mulberry32), no Math.random, +Y up, 1u=1m.

architecture_kit.summary: ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED with one added connective piece and one clarified convention. An original modular mid-century film-STUDIO kit-of-parts (14 grid-snapping modules): soundstage shell (corrugated wall, elephant-door bay, barrel-vault + ridge-monitor roof, corner+parapet cap), mill/workshop (sawtooth north-light, low brick wall), admin (stucco two-story bay), commissary (streamline curved-corner pavilion), backlot false-front street flat, boundary wall + pier, marquee entrance gate, loading dock + canopy, water-tower landmark, PLUS a new plain-lot ground-tile module for the apron/street plane. Grid: primary snap module M = 2 m (all wall-family pieces 2 m wide, 0.20 m thick, origin lower-left-back corner on the ground plane); coarse structural BAY = 8 m (4 M) governs stage shell + elephant door so stages come out at 16/24/32 m footprints. Course lines fixed at 3 m (story), 4 m (low shed), 6 m (two-story), 8 m (stage). Low-poly stylized (full soundstage shell ~1,000-1,400 tris; whole unique-kit geometry ~3,910 tris, well under the ~6,250-tri Lab 04 lot norm since instances are free). Function-coded procedural PBR only, warm golden-hour, +Y up, 1u=1m. Architecture carries NO skeleton — the 65-bone Mannequin constraint applies only to crew.

items.name: M-01 Soundstage Wall Panel (corrugated bay)
items.description: Workhorse blank exterior stage panel: flat 2 m-wide x 8 m-tall x 0.20 m-thick, vertical corrugated steel via HM.wall (corrugated height->normal, ribs=46). Shallow rivet band + base flashing as thin extruded strips (silhouette, not decal). Single-quad dark interior back-face (HM.darkMetal) so cut-open interiors aren't hollow. Origin lower-left-back on ground; edge-snaps on 2 m grid; four = one 8 m bay. Leanest piece, repeated most.

items.name: M-02 Elephant-Door Bay
items.description: Signature 8 m (4 M) structural bay with the giant sliding scenery door: 0.3 m recessed reveal, two overlapping horizontally-ribbed leaves via HM.doorLeaf (large ribs, ribs=10, distinct from wall), top guide rail + bottom floor track as thin strips, a painted STAGE __ number field (signMaterial). A human-scale personnel door cut into the left leaf sells the 8 m scale. Two 8 m corner pilasters flank, aligned to M-01 edges. Door clear 6 m W x 6 m H.

items.name: M-03 Barrel-Vault Roof + Ridge Monitor (per bay)
items.description: Classic soundstage roof, authored per 8 m bay: shallow barrel vault (HM.roof, ribs=70 lifted-black metal) capped by a raised clerestory ridge-monitor with slatted louver fins (thin extrusions) and a flat felt top (M.roofFelt). End-cap tympanum quad option closes end bays. Sits on the 8 m top course; repeats for 2/3/4-bay continuous vault. Keeps a repeated stage from reading as a flat box.

items.name: M-04 Stage Corner + Parapet Cap
items.description: Clean 90deg vertical corner (2x2 m L pilaster, slightly proud, warm accent M.accent) tying two wall runs + a thin 2 m parapet coping (M.concrete) that snaps end-to-end and turns corners. Includes a small low-poly rooftop HVAC/vent box + stub exhaust placed by the assembler. Without this a repeated wall run can't honestly turn a corner.

items.name: M-05 Sawtooth Mill/Workshop Roof Bay (north-light)
items.description: Scenery-shop serrated north-light sawtooth: one asymmetric tooth per 2 m module, a slanted solid roof plane (M.roofFelt) + a glazed clerestory (M.glass, thin mullion strips) on the vertical north side. Runs on 2 m over M-06 low walls to make a mill of any length; faces one direction so glazing catches sky. Strongest 'working studio not office park' cue after the stages.

items.name: M-06 Low Shop Wall Panel (brick + clerestory)
items.description: General industrial low wall for mill/warehouse/service: 2 m W x 4 m H x 0.20 m, brick (M.brick) with an optional high clerestory window band (M.glass + thin frame) above reach. Two variants share one footprint (solid brick / brick+clerestory). Snaps to M-01/M-04 on 2 m; carries M-05 sawtooth or a monopitch. 4 m height gives honest variety against 8 m stages.

items.name: M-07 Admin/Office Wall Bay (stucco, two-story)
items.description: Public civic front: 2 m W x 6 m H (two 3 m stories), warm stucco (M.wallCream / M.wallWarm), a recessed steel-frame window per story (M.glass + mullions + sill + drip lintel), slender pilaster reveals at edges for a rhythmic Deco/streamline facade. Stepped-parapet coping variant caps the top. A ground-floor ENTRANCE variant (double door + canopy stub + STUDIO NAME signMaterial field) anchors the run.

items.name: M-08 Commissary Corner Pavilion (streamline, curved end)
items.description: Distinct landmark shell (not a wall family): 4 m streamline-moderne pavilion, one rounded curved-plan corner bay (8-segment low-poly arc), a continuous ribbon window (M.glass band wrapping the curve), flat parapet with a raised COMMISSARY name band (signMaterial), small flat entry canopy. Smooth stucco + terracotta base course (M.accent). Footprint 8x6 m on the 2 m grid; the one deliberate break in the orthogonal rhythm.

items.name: M-09 Backlot False-Front Facade Flat
items.description: The 'movies are faked here' piece: 2 m W x ~5 m period street elevation (shop window+door, upper windows, cornice via signMaterial/painted-wall), with NOTHING behind but exposed diagonal wood bracing + a catwalk stub (M.trunk/M.crate) so the back honestly reads as a standing set. Variants share the 2 m footprint (shopfront/townhouse/saloon); alternate heights 4.5/5/5.5 m for a non-flat roofline. Near-flat front keeps it very cheap.
items.approx_dims_m: 2.0 W x 0.15 D front + 0.8 D bracing x 4.5-5.5 H

items.name: M-10 Boundary Wall Section + Pier
items.description: Studio boundary/property-line wall: 2 m L x 3 m H solid (stucco M.wallWarm, concrete cap M.concrete) with a slightly-proud square pier every module for a rhythmic buttressed shadow. Snaps end-to-end on 2 m; corner-pier variant turns 90deg. One variant carries a painted MERIDIAN PICTURES crest band beside the gate. Leanest run-piece so it wraps the whole perimeter cheaply.

items.name: M-11 Marquee Entrance Gate (2-bay hero)
items.description: Signature arrival landmark: two tall stucco piers flanking a 6 m vehicle opening (grid-aligned), joined by a horizontal marquee beam carrying an EMISSIVE MERIDIAN PICTURES sign band (practical() emissive) + a Deco crest, plus a pedestrian gate leaf + a lowerable boom-barrier stub. Piers snap flush to M-10 runs as the one grand break in the perimeter. The piece a viewer photographs; justifies its budget.
items.approx_dims_m: 10.0 W (6.0 opening) x 1.0 D x 6.0 H

items.name: M-12 Loading Dock + Canopy Attachment
items.description: Connective 'active building' piece: raised concrete dock platform (1.2 m truck-bed height, M.concrete) with a stepped end, short stairs, bollards/curb, and a cantilevered monopitch canopy on slim posts (HM.roof corrugated, matching M-01). Sits flush against one 8 m bay (under M-02 or M-06) on the 2 m grid; also freestanding. Human-scale steps sell the 8 m doors above.

items.name: M-13 Water Tower (standalone landmark)
items.description: The most recognizable studio silhouette: four splayed steel legs + thin cross-bracing struts on a 4x4 m base, a low-poly 10-12-segment cylindrical tank with a name band (signMaterial), shallow conical roof + finial. ~14 m to tank top so it reads over the stage roofline. Placed once as the campus focal point; the tall thin profile a wide establishing shot resolves to first.

items.name: M-14 Lot Ground Tile (apron / street / plaza) [ADDED]
items.description: ADDED so the assembly has an honest ground plane instead of assuming a scene floor: a flat 8x8 m (4 M x 4 M) ground module in three material presets on one mesh slot (SWAP not remodel) — apron concrete (HM.concrete board-formed w/ expansion joints), lot asphalt (HM.asphalt tiled dark), and plaza paving. Optional hazard-hatch / keep-clear decal quad (hazardTexture) and chalk marks (markTexture) as separate thin overlay quads. Tiles on the 2 m grid; the surface the crew, props, and dolly track sit on. Keeps the kit self-contained for the vertical slice.

materials_used: corrugated-metal HM.wall/HM.roof/HM.doorLeaf (heightToNormal(corrugatedHeight) — stage walls fine ribs, door leaves large ribs, roof fine ribs; canvas + height->normal, no downloaded texture)
brick M.brick (low shop/warehouse/mill walls M-06)
stucco / warm painted wall M.wallCream + M.wallWarm (admin M-07, commissary M-08, boundary M-10, gate piers M-11)
concrete M.concrete + HM.concrete (dock M-12, parapet/caps M-04/M-10, ground tile M-14, base plinth)
wood / board M.trunk + M.crate (false-front bracing + catwalks M-09, mill trim)
roof tile / felt M.roofFelt (barrel-vault + monitor tops M-03, sawtooth solid planes M-05, flat parapet roofs)
glass M.glass (steel-frame windows M-07, clerestories M-05/M-06, ribbon window M-08, false-front shop glass M-09)
brass / painted-steel accent M.brass + M.accent (corner pilasters M-04, canopy posts, gate details, dock bollards)
emissive sign band via practical() + signMaterial/makeSignTexture (marquee M-11 name band, stage-number fields M-02, admin name field M-07, water-tower band M-13)

architecture_kit.notes: REFINEMENTS vs the submitted spec: (1) ADDED M-14 Lot Ground Tile (+24 tris, +1 module) so the vertical slice does not depend on an external scene floor — the kit is now self-contained and the crew/props/dolly-track have an authored surface. New unique-geometry total 3,910 tris (was 3,830), still far under the ~6,250 Lab 04 whole-lot norm because filling a lot uses free instances. (2) CLARIFIED every material name maps to a REAL export in src/lab/materials.ts (M.*) and src/lab/heroMaterials.ts (HM.*, practical, signMaterial, hazardTexture, markTexture) verified in-repo — no new material family is invented. GRID/SNAP spec unchanged: M=2 m wall family, BAY=8 m stage shell, course lines 3/4/6/8 m, origin lower-left-back on ground, roof/cap pieces snap to top course. SNAP SETS: {M-01,M-02,M-04}=stage walls (+M-03 caps); {M-06,M-05,M-12}=mill/shop; {M-07}=admin run; {M-09}=false-front street; {M-10,M-11}=perimeter; standalones {M-08,M-13}; {M-14} ground under all. MINIMUM BELIEVABLE ASSEMBLY (proves the kit): one 24x16 m Stage 1 (M-01 perimeter + 2x M-04 corners + 1x M-02 front + 3x M-03 roof + 1x M-12 dock), a short mill (M-06 under 6x M-05 teeth), a 3-bay M-07 admin front w/ entrance, a 5-module M-09 false-front street, M-08 commissary, M-10 perimeter w/ M-11 gate, M-13 water tower, all on an M-14 ground field. RIG NOTE: none of these 14 modules is a character; they carry no skeleton and need none — the 65-bone Mannequin constraint is crew-only, flagged here to confirm it was considered and is out of scope. STYLE: silhouette survives materials-stripped (the 'less boxy' geometry win); function-coded procedural PBR; warm golden-hour; human-scaled details (M-02 personnel door, M-12 steps, M-09 shopfronts) sell the 8 m stage doors. ORIGINALITY: film-studio vocabulary (elephant doors, ridge monitors, sawtooth mill, marquee gate, false-fronts w/ exposed bracing, water tower) — NOT a generic downtown kit. ISOLATION: architecture only; no crew/props/mechanics. Design spec; no bpy code written per task.

props.summary: ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED. A 12-entry set (10 single props + 2 kits, ~5,170 tris) for a working soundstage: studio camera on tripod/dolly, fresnel spotlight on stand, C-stand w/ grip arm, apple-box+sandbag kit, cable reel + coil, director's chair (0.45 m seat for Sitting_* clips), flag/scrim/silk frame kit, boom mic, clapperboard, megaphone, straight dolly-track module. Every item buildable in bpy from primitives (bevelled boxes, 6-12-sided cylinders/cones, tapered prisms, low-subdiv icospheres, flat quads, one torus for the cable coil); no sculpt, no booleans (hand-holes/hinges faked with inset dark faces + texture to stay manifold); fine detail is texture not geometry. All materials map to the real repo family. Total 5,170 tris sits under the ~6,250 whole-lot norm. The three required hand props (clapperboard, boom, megaphone) are pivoted at the natural hand-grip and attach-tagged to ride the verified hand_l / hand_r bones of the 65-bone Mannequin with the 43-clip library unchanged.

items.name: Studio Camera on Tripod + Dolly
items.description: Hero centerpiece: stylized mid-century 35mm studio camera (Mitchell BNC / Technicolor-blimp read). THREE separately-parented sub-objects — (A) camera body, (B) tripod OR crab-dolly base, (C) optional operator seat — so they pose independently. Body = rounded/bevelled box blimp ~0.55x0.35x0.65 m + stubby 8-10-sided lens barrel (0.14 dia x 0.20) + a 10-sided film-magazine drum (0.30 dia) top-rear + a viewfinder box + two 6-sided focus knobs. Tripod = 3 tapered wooden legs (spread ~0.9 m), triangular spreader, bowl/head cylinder; lens axis ~1.5 m. Dolly = flat steel deck 1.0x0.7x0.08 + center column + 4 low caster cylinders (non-rolling) + swept push-bar. A tiny red-eye emissive quad reads 'recording'.
items.approx_dims_m: Body 0.55W x 0.65D x 0.40H; tripod ~0.9 dia, lens axis ~1.5H; dolly deck 1.0 x 0.7 x 0.08 (push-bar ~1.05H)

items.name: Fresnel Spotlight on Stand (Junior/Baby)
items.description: Signature lighting unit + primary golden-hour source, instanced widely. Posable lamp head + rolling stand. Head = 8-10-sided cylindrical/conical housing (0.30 dia x 0.35) + a shallow bezel holding the stepped fresnel lens (flat disc, 2-3 concentric ring loop cuts, ridges faked in texture); 4 barn-door quad flaps hinged at the bezel, posed slightly open; a 2-arm yoke cradling the head to tilt; focus knob + cable gland. Stand = 6-sided telescoping pole (2 diameter steps), cast collar, 3 folding legs on caster cylinders. Head center 1.6-2.0 m. Warm EMISSIVE lens via practical() glows amber when hot; on/off is a material swap, no geometry change.

items.name: C-Stand (Century Stand) with Grip Arm

props.notes: ACCEPTED with no geometry changes. Every material name is confirmed against real exports: src/lab/materials.ts (M.darkMetal, M.brass, M.trunk, M.crate, M.glass, M.signDark, M.wallCream, M.accent, signMaterial/makeSignTexture) and src/lab/heroMaterials.ts (HM.*, HERO.*, practical(), markTexture, hazardTexture, mulberry32, heightToNormal). HAND-ATTACHABLE PROPS: clapperboard, boom, megaphone are pivoted at the natural hand-grip and attach-tagged (Prop_<name>_attach_hand_[lr]) so each parents to hand_l / hand_r of the VERIFIED 65-bone Mannequin with an identity offset and rides Interact / PickUp_Table / Idle_Talking_Loop / Idle_Loop / Walk_Loop unchanged; the director's chair seat at 0.45 m supports Sitting_Enter/Idle/Exit. BUILDABILITY: primitives only, no sculpt, no booleans (hand-holes/hinges faked with inset dark faces + texture to stay manifold), all fine detail (fresnel steps, clapper stripes, slate fields, net scrims, stencils, wood grain) is TEXTURE not geometry. SWAP-NOT-REMODEL variants (crew vs DIRECTOR chair; flag/scrim/silk; vintage vs modern megaphone; on/off fresnel + camera tally; wood vs steel reel) are material/name swaps on a shared mesh slot. SCALE real-world metric 1u=1m, +Y up. ISOLATION: design spec only, R&D asset-lab proposal, no mechanics/economy; no bpy code written per task.

vertical_slice: "Stage 1, Golden Hour — Setup for a Take": a single ~24x16 m soundstage (M-01 corrugated perimeter + 2x M-04 corners + 1x M-02 elephant-door front with a painted STAGE 1 field + 3x M-03 barrel-vault/ridge-monitor roof bays + 1x M-12 loading dock) sitting on an M-14 concrete apron tile, with the M-13 water tower behind it catching the low warm key over the stage roofline, and a slice of M-10 boundary wall with the M-11 marquee gate reading in the mid-ground for studio identity. On the apron in front of the open elephant door: the hero Studio Camera on its crab dolly riding a 2-module run of Straight Dolly Track, a Fresnel Spotlight (emissive lens ON, warm) and a C-Stand carrying a 24x36 SILK frame flagging the key, an Apple Box stack + Sandbag weighing the stand, a Cable Reel with a loose coil snaking to the light, and a Director's Chair (DIRECTOR back) at the apron edge. CREW (the locked Grounded Studio Crew, ~2k tris each, replacing the tinted raw mannequin): a Director in the chair playing Sitting_Idle_Loop holding the Megaphone (attach_hand_r); a Camera/DP at the eyepiece; a Grip playing Push_Loop on the dolly; an Electric/Gaffer walking cable (Walk_Loop, shoulder coil); a PA playing Idle_Talking_Loop with a clipboard; a Carpenter kneeling at a set piece (Fixing_Kneeling); a Boom operator holding the fishpole overhead (Idle_Loop, boom attach_hand_l); a second crew member entering (Sitting_Enter at a second chair). The slice's PURPOSE is to prove, in one frame under the existing ACES + RoomEnvironment golden-hour rig: (1) crew read as a working film crew by SILHOUETTE + costume, not tint, at management-orbit distance; (2) all six roles are distinguishable; (3) the stress clips (Sitting_*, Fixing_Kneeling, Push_Loop, Walk_Loop, Idle_Talking_Loop) play with clean deformation and no prop/hat/cable float on the hybrid rig; (4) hand-attached props ride correctly; (5) crew + kit + props all sit in ONE warm palette so an inhabited backlot reads as one authored world and stays draw-call-cheap via shared materials. Capture proof PNGs of this frame per role per stress clip (capture-*.mjs + window.__lab)."
naming_conventions:
"MESHES: <Kind>_<Name>[_<Variant>] PascalCase. Architecture modules keep their kit IDs: Arch_M01_StageWall, Arch_M02_ElephantDoor, Arch_M03_BarrelRoof, ... Arch_M14_GroundTile (+ variant suffix, e.g. Arch_M06_ShopWall_Clerestory, Arch_M07_AdminBay_Entrance, Arch_M09_FalseFront_Saloon). Props: Prop_<Name>[_<Variant>], e.g. Prop_StudioCamera, Prop_Fresnel, Prop_CStand, Prop_AppleBox_Full/_Half/_Quarter/_Pancake, Prop_Sandbag, Prop_CableReel, Prop_DirectorsChair / Prop_DirectorsChair_Director, Prop_GripFrame_18x24 (+ fabric preset in material, not name), Prop_DollyTrack_Straight.

HAND-ATTACHABLE PROPS carry an explicit attach tag naming the target bone: Prop_<Name>_attach_<bone>, e.g. Prop_Slate_attach_hand_l, Prop_Boom_attach_hand_l, Prop_Megaphone_attach_hand_r. The tag means: pivot/origin is at the natural grip so parenting to that exact 65-bone Mannequin bone with an identity offset lands correctly.

CHARACTERS: Char_<Role>[_<BuildSize>], e.g. Char_Grip_Standard, Char_Director_Heavy, Char_CameraDP_Standard, Char_Electric_Standard, Char_PA_Standard, Char_Carpenter_Standard. Roles are DATA (a role-config table -> {coat/vest/apron shell, headwear, belt kit, shoulder prop, palette swatch}); a new role is a row, not a new model.

BONES / VERTEX GROUPS: NEVER renamed — every vertex group matches a real Mannequin bone name EXACTLY (root, pelvis, spine_01/02/03, neck_01, Head, clavicle/upperarm/lowerarm/hand_[lr], the 5 finger chains incl. *_04_leaf, thigh/calf/foot/ball/ball_leaf_[lr]). Costume/prop weights reference only these existing names.

MATERIALS: reference the real repo exports by their code name in comments/manifests — M.* (materials.ts) and HM.* / HERO.* / practical / signMaterial / markTexture / hazardTexture (heroMaterials.ts). No new material family invented; character-specific slots are named skin, cloth_work_<dept>, leather, headwear_felt, hardhat_amber, face_albedo.

LOD SUFFIX: _LOD0 / _LOD1 / _LOD2 appended to the mesh name; all LODs of one asset share the identical bone-named vertex groups so one animation instance drives any LOD.

GENERAL: 1 unit = 1 m; +Y up on glTF export; triangulated; single skin per character; deterministic seeds only (mulberry32), no Math.random."
lod_collision_standard:
"LOD (three tiers, ALL sharing the same 65-bone armature + identical vertex-group names so one animation instance drives any LOD and clips are never re-authored):

CHARACTERS — LOD0 (hero/mid-shot, ~2.0-2.2k tris): full segment-island body + costume shell + headwear + painted-face ovoid + mitt hands + signature prop. LOD1 (mid-ground, ~900-1,100 tris): merge costume into the body silhouette (fewer loops), hands to a plain mitt, shoulder-cable/clipboard to a single slab, keep role silhouette + hat + face texture. LOD2 (background crowd, ~350-500 tris): single fused body+costume shell, head a 3-ring ovoid still carrying the face texture, hat a 6-gon disc, no separate hands/props — role still readable by silhouette + palette. LOD swap NEVER touches animation.

ARCHITECTURE — LOD0 = as authored (silhouette detail: rivet bands, louver fins, mullions, monitor). LOD1 (~50-60%): drop thin extruded strips, mullions become texture, louvers a single slab. LOD2 (~25-35%): building reduced to its box+roof silhouette with materials only. Instances are free — the whole lot stays under the ~6,250-tri Lab 04 norm by instancing, not unique meshes.

PROPS — LOD0 as authored; LOD1 drop cylinder sides (8->6), grooves/steps become texture; LOD2 minimal capped boxes/cones, single-material, no fine geo. Hand-attached props keep LOD0 near-camera (they're held close), LOD1/2 only in crowd/far.

DRAW-CALL DISCIPLINE (the labs' proven lever): share ONE material set across all crew and all instances of a kit/prop so a populated backlot stays draw-call-bound-affordable on the software renderer; per-instance variation is vertex color / material tint, not a new material.

COLLISION (R&D-lab convention, presentation-only — no game physics implied): each asset ships with a SEPARATE low-poly convex collision proxy named <MeshName>_col, NOT the render mesh. Characters: a single upright capsule ~0.44 m wide x 1.80 m tall (no per-limb collision — animation-visual only). Architecture: an axis-aligned box or a few boxes matching the footprint + wall planes on the 2 m grid (stage = one box shell with the elephant-door opening as a gap; boundary wall = thin box run). Props: one convex box/cylinder per prop matching the bounding footprint (dolly track = a thin flat box the dolly rides; C-stand/light = a base-footprint cylinder + a thin column box). Ground tiles: a flat thin box. Hand-attached props carry NO collision (they inherit the character). All collision proxies are convex, low-poly (<50 tris), and separate from render + LOD meshes so they never affect the tri budget. This is a spec convention for downstream use; no collision/physics is BUILT in this lab (isolation)."
open_risks: A-pose authoring is mandatory and unforgiving: the appended rig carries large baked LOCAL bone rotations (measured upperarm_l 93.7deg, clavicle_l 102.8deg, thigh_l 165.9deg, pelvis 104.5deg). All geometry MUST be generated from each bone's evaluated bind-pose WORLD matrix (bone.matrix_world), never from a hand-authored joint-position table — bone ROLL, not just position, governs mesh orientation. Any island built in a naive T-pose or at raw joint coordinates will bind twisted or pinch at the shoulder. This is the single highest-risk step and the reason the build order in the character bible is non-negotiable.

Rigid-segment interpenetration at deep flexion: the hybrid's near-rigid islands (adopted for bind safety) can cosmetically self-intersect thigh/calf/torso at Sitting_Enter/Exit, deep Fixing_Kneeling, Crouch_Idle_Loop, and Driving_Loop. Accepted as the stylized signature at management-orbit distance, but MUST be verified against the actual clips (the stress subset), not assumed. Size the 1.5-2 cm joint overlap for the worst-case clip angle.

Additive costume shells (long coat, shoulder cable coil, apron) can clip the body or float during extreme clips. Mitigate by weighting each shell to the SAME bones as the limb it overlays and keeping it snug; the 43-clip playback (esp. Sitting_*, Fixing_Kneeling, Driving_Loop) is the gate. Worst case a role uses only shells proven safe for its clip set.

Hand mitts must weight to hand_[lr] (+ first knuckle) ONLY, never the *_04_leaf finger bones which carry 90deg twists — otherwise PickUp_Table / Interact / Push_Loop splay the paddle. Verify in the stress set.

Painted-ovoid face can look flat at extreme close range — accepted per the house 'stylized believable, not photoreal' line; cameras stay at crew distance in this lab. If a true hero close-up is ever needed that is a separate concept, out of scope.

Un-meshed finger bones are a bet that no REQUIRED crew clip needs visible finger articulation. TRUE for the crew set (idle/walk/carry/fix/push/sit/drive/talk) per the verified 43-clip roster, but the bet must be re-checked, not assumed, if the role/clip set expands.
Draw-call blow-up with many instances — mitigate by sharing one material/atlas across all crew + kit + props (the labs' proven discipline) and by LOD2 for crowds; verify on the software renderer.

No bpy code exists yet — this is a DESIGN SPEC only per the task. The armature-append + world-matrix build path, the segment-island + overlap-blend skinning, and the full 43-clip verification gate are specified but UNPROVEN until the generator is written and run headless. The verification gate (capture PNGs per role per stress clip, assert 65 bones unchanged) is the thing that turns this spec from plausible to proven; treat sign-off as blocked until that gate passes.

Scope/isolation: character bible, kit, and props are visual R&D assets only. Any pull toward chemistry, aging, career visuals, schedules, economy, or LLM features is a HARD non-goal — stop and report rather than build. This spec opens no Gate and touches no protected branch/spike; it is not a merge.
